answer: One defense is bonded stake tied to real work. Each agent must lock collateral to act, so spinning up a thousand fake identities is like trying to populate every barren tundra at once: the capital cost scales linearly with the swarm. An honest agent is an island of reputation built slowly across an ocean of verified transactions, while a sybil fleet forfeits its bonds the moment peers detect collusion, making the attack far more expensive than any gain.
